# Normative Precedence Contract

Deep Redact resolves overlapping targeting rules with one public total order:

`exact string-path` > `structured path` > `exact key` > `regex property` > `substring`

## Overlap Matrix

| Higher-precedence rule | Lower-precedence rule | Winner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact string-path` | `structured path` | `exact string-path` |
| `exact string-path` | `exact key` | `exact string-path` |
| `exact string-path` | `regex property` | `exact string-path` |
| `exact string-path` | `substring` | `exact string-path` |
| `structured path` | `exact key` | `structured path` |
| `structured path` | `regex property` | `structured path` |
| `structured path` | `substring` | `structured path` |
| `exact key` | `regex property` | `exact key` |
| `exact key` | `substring` | `exact key` |
| `regex property` | `substring` | `regex property` |

## Additional Rules

- When exact string-path rules overlap in the same layer, the more specific canonical exact string-path wins over the less specific canonical exact string-path.
- When duplicate selectors collapse to the same canonical path within one layer, initialisation fails rather than choosing a runtime winner.
- Whole-value censoring or removal wins over substring replacement.
- `retainStructure: true` preserves the matched container and keeps descendant targeting active unless a higher-precedence whole-value rule has already claimed that descendant.

## Worked Examples

### path-versus-key

A canonical exact string-path rule claims the leaf before the exact key rule or substring replacement can run.

Input fixture:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: "token=path",
  },
}
```

Configuration:

```ts
{
  censor: keySourceMarker,
  keys: [
    "secret",
    /^secret$/,
  ],
  paths: [
    {
      path: "account.secret",
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
    },
  ],
  stringTests: [
    {
      pattern: /token=[^&\s]+/,
      replacer: tokenSubstringMarker,
    },
  ],
}
```

Expected output:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
  },
}
```

### retain-structure-descendant-targeting

A retained exact string-path keeps the container shape, lets a descendant structured path win, and still claims descendants with no higher direct rule.

Input fixture:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: {
      value: "token=secret",
    },
    inherited: "token=inherited",
    note: "token=note",
  },
  free: "token=free",
}
```

Configuration:

```ts
{
  censor: keySourceMarker,
  keys: [
    "note",
  ],
  paths: [
    {
      path: "account",
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
      retainStructure: true,
    },
    {
      path: [
        "account",
        "secret",
        /^value$/,
      ],
      censor: "[STRUCTURED-PATH]",
    },
  ],
  stringTests: [
    {
      pattern: /token=[^&\s]+/,
      replacer: tokenSubstringMarker,
    },
  ],
}
```

Expected output:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: {
      value: "[STRUCTURED-PATH]",
    },
    inherited: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
    note: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
  },
  free: "token=[SUBSTRING]",
}
```

### duplicate-canonical-path-init-failure

Differently written selectors that canonicalise to the same exact path fail before runtime resolution.

Input fixture:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: "token=duplicate",
  },
}
```

Configuration:

```ts
{
  paths: [
    {
      path: "account.secret",
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
    },
    {
      path: [
        "account",
        "secret",
      ],
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH]",
    },
  ],
}
```

Expected initialisation error:

```text
Duplicate canonical selector "account.secret" already defined at options.paths[0].path.
```

### exact-string-path-specificity

The retained parent keeps descendants reachable while the more specific exact string-path claims its own leaf.

Input fixture:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: "token=secret",
    sibling: "token=sibling",
  },
}
```

Configuration:

```ts
{
  paths: [
    {
      path: "account",
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH:PARENT]",
      retainStructure: true,
    },
    {
      path: "account.secret",
      censor: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH:DESCENDANT]",
    },
  ],
}
```

Expected output:

```ts
{
  account: {
    secret: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH:DESCENDANT]",
    sibling: "[EXACT-STRING-PATH:PARENT]",
  },
}
```

### regex-property-versus-substring
